title: $\varphi$TD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions
claim: A family of our distributional variants matches or beats the baseline across diverse environments, showing the approach's flexibility and robustness.
layout: 4 panels in one row, shared legend, shaded confidence bands
description: A single row of four line-plot panels showing learning curves on the MinAtar environments Asterix, Breakout, Freeway and SpaceInvaders. The x-axis is environment steps (up to 1e7) and the y-axis is episode return, shown only on the leftmost panel. Each panel has eight curves with distinct markers and colors: a black PQN baseline and seven φTD variants (Gaussian, Gamma, Laplace, Categorical, Quantile, Dirac, Cauchy). Translucent shaded bands show 95% confidence intervals. A legend sits inside the Asterix panel. Most φTD variants climb together and end above or near PQN. Exceptions include Freeway, where PQN rises fastest, and the Categorical and Gamma variants, which lag in several panels. The eye goes first to the black PQN line and the tight bundle of colorful curves.
caption: MinAtar evaluation results. Mean episodic returns evaluated over 10M training steps across all four MinAtar environments. Results are aggregated over 5 independent random seeds, with the shaded areas representing the 95% confidence intervals under Gaussian assumption.
abstract: Distributional Reinforcement Learning methods aim to learn the entire distribution of returns, yet current algorithmic approaches are limited to a narrow class of distributions. We propose $Ï$TD, a method to overcome this limitation by computing the loss in the frequency domain. We demonstrate that this further unifies quantile and categorical approaches to distributional RL, and enables the learning of distributions that were previously impossible to capture, such as mixtures of continuous distributions. We empirically study $Ï$TD, across synthetic benchmarks and large-scale deep RL environments and demonstrate that the flexibility obtained from wider parametric families can lead to improved performance.
